entries.toelichting: Third part of the night as watch-period (Ex 14:24; Judg 7:19; 1Sam 11:11; Ps 63:7; 90:4; Lam 2:19). Hyphenated to preserve the night-watch-interval; family with H8104 shamar 'guard'.
Judg-through-the-window-Sisera's-mother-looked-out-through-the-lattice and Prov-so-I-saw-through-my-window-through-my-lattice (Judg 5:28; Prov 7:6). Hyphenated.
Josh-Eshtaol-Zorah-Ashnah and Josh-Iphtah-Ashnah-Nezib (Josh 15:33,43). Hyphenated.
Proper noun, Judah-hill-country-city; Josh 15:52; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Eshan.
Diviner or magician - in Daniel 1:20 (above all the magicians and astrologers in his whole kingdom) and Daniel 2:2 (the king commanded to call the magicians and astrologers); court-class.
Professional-magician at Babylonian court (Dan 1:20; 2:2,10,27; 4:4; 5:7,11,15). Hyphenated to distinguish the enchant-magic-aspect from H2748 chartom 'magician' and H3784 kashaf 'practise-sorcery'.
Carrying-case for arrows of archer (Job 39:23; Ps 127:5; Isa 22:6; 49:2; Jer 5:16; Lam 3:13). Hyphenated to preserve the arrows-case-aspect.
Proper noun, Babylonian eunuch-commander Daniel-context; Dan 1:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ashpenaz.

2S-and-he-distributed-to-all-the-people-of-Israel-a-cake-of-bread-and-a-good-portion-of-meat-and-a-flagon-of-wine and 1Chr-and-he-distributed-to-each-one-of-Israel-a-cake-of-bread-and-a-good-portion-of-meat-and-a-flagon-of-wine.
Refuse-rubble-mound outside the city-gate (1Sam 2:8; Neh 2:13; 3:13,14; Ps 113:7; Lam 4:5). Hyphenated to preserve the rubble-rubbish-aspect.
Philistine coastal-city (Judg 1:18, 1Sam 6:17, 2Sam 1:20, Jer 25:20, 47:5-7, Amos 1:8, Zeph 2:4-7, Zech 9:5); concordantly transliterated.
Inhabitant of Ashkelon-Philistine; Josh 13:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ashkelonite.
Piel: declare to be blessed; the hyphenated English marks the action (distinguished from ashar II 'set-paces').
Root 'shr (go-straight, connect). Pan-functional relative. English 'which' covers the relative function broadly; 'that', 'who' are grammatical variants of the same relative.
Conjunction-use of asher: 'that, where, because'; the hyphenated English distinguishes from rel.pron.
Preposition-use of asher (mostly 'me-asher' = 'from-what'); the hyphenated English distinguishes from rel.pron and conjunction.
Compound ke+asher. Comparative/temporal conjunction. 'As' covers both functions.
Exclamation-noun 'blessed is...'; distinguished from barak (bless) and berakhah (blessing); concordantly 'blessed-II'.
Proper noun; son and tribe of Israel; concordantly transliterated.
Prosperity-state; Asher-name-explanation; Gen 30:13.
Footsteps on the way, figuratively conduct of life (Job 31:7; Ps 17:5; 37:31; 44:19; 73:2; Prov 14:15; Isa 58:13). Hyphenated to mark footprint; distinguished from H6541 par'os 'single-step'.

The people or tribe over which Ish-bosheth was made king - 2Samuel 2:9 (over Gilead, over the Ashurites, over Jezreel); possibly Asher-tribe-variant; Ezekiel 27:6 (your decks they have made of cypress).
Proper noun, Cyprian-cypress-species ship-deck; Eze 27:6; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bath-ashurim.
Proper noun, son of Jehallelel-Judah-branch; 1Chr 4:16; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Asarel.
Proper noun, Levi-singer son of Asaph; 1Chr 25:2; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Asarelah.
Canaanite fertility-goddess, also her cult-pole; concordantly transliterated (no English equivalent).
Patronym-clan tribe Asher; Judg 1:32; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Asherite.
Asriel-son-of-Gilead and Manassite tribe-head (Num 26:31; Josh 17:2; 1Chr 7:14). English convention: Asriel. 'I-am-rejoiced-by-God' or 'God-is-prosperity'.
Patronym-clan son of Manasseh; Num 26:31; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Asrielite.
The foundation-walls of the rebuilt temple about which Tattenai reported to Darius - Ezra 5:3, 5:9; Aramaic Persian loanword, possibly panel-work or wooden frame.
City on the border of Judah and Dan, Samson's camp (Josh 15:33; 19:41; Judg 13:25; 16:31; 18:2,8,11; 1Chr 2:53). English convention: Eshtaol.
Patronym-clan from Eshtaol; 1Chr 2:53; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Eshtaolite.
Aramaic rebellion-uprising (Ezra 4:15,19 Jerusalem-accusation); word-stem uncertain, possibly Persian-loan.
1Chr-and-Mehir-begat-Eshton and 1Chr-and-Eshton-begat-Beth-Rapha-and-Paseah-and-Tehinnah-the-father-of-Ir-Nahash (1Chr 4:11,12). Hyphenated.
Priestly-city in Judah's hill-country (Josh 15:50; 21:14; 1Sam 30:28; 1Chr 4:17,19; 6:57). English convention: Eshtemoa.

Dan-aramaic-signs-of-the-Most-High and Dan-aramaic-great-signs-and-wonders and Dan-aramaic-signs-Nebuchadnezzar (Dan 3:32,33; 6:28). Hyphenated to distinguish the sign-wonder-aramaic-aspect from H226 ot.

Nota accusativi. Marks the determinate direct object; no lexical content, purely syntactic. Concordantly rendered as the untranslated sign « to keep the particle visible without adding English semantics.

Preposition of accompaniment, homograph with the nota accusativi (H853) but functionally distinct. 'With' is the standard equivalent; semantically overlaps with im (H5973a) but etymologically distinct.

Iron implement for plough or digging (1Sam 13:20,21; Isa 2:4; Jer 26:15; Mic 4:3; Joel 4:10). Hyphenated to preserve the plowshare-mattock-aspect; distinguished from homonym H853 eth-I (accusative-marker).
Proper noun, Sidonian king father of Jezebel; 1Kgs 16:31; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ethbaal.
Aramaic/poetic Hebrew: approach, come; parallel to bo; concordantly 'come-aramaic'.
Aramaic verb: approach, arrive; parallel to Hebrew bo; concordantly compound with language-marker.
Personal pronoun 2ms. 'You' is kernel-form (English does not distinguish singular/plural in modern usage; thou/thee are archaic).
Pers.pron. 2sg. feminine: you (addressing Ruth, bride in Song); the hyphenated English marks gender.
Second-person singular feminine; concordantly 'you-woman' to mark gender explicitly (H859a = masculine, H859b = generic).
Personal pronoun 2mp. Counterpart of atah (H859a). 'You-plural' standard.
Second-person feminine-plural personal-pronoun (Gen 31:6; Eze 13:11,20; 34:17,31). Hyphenated to distinguish the feminine-plural-pronoun-aspect from H859d 'you-plural' (masc.).
Female riding-animal, calm and valuable; concordantly 'she-donkey' (distinguished from chamor donkey).
Aramaic-specific term for fire-heated-furnace - exclusively in Daniel 3:6,11,15,17,19-23,26 'fiery-furnace-burning of-fire' - actually built-furnace into which Shadrach-Meshach-Abednego-were-cast.
First-sense attuq; temple-gallery-closed spaces; Eze 41:15.
Second-sense attiq; closed gallery-passage; Eze 41:15.
Philistine-mercenary who remained loyal to David (2Sam 15:19,21,22; 18:2,5,12; 23:29). 'Near-me'. English convention: Ittai.
Wilderness-edge-place on exodus-route (Ex 13:20; Num 33:6,7,8). English convention: Etham. 'Boundary-post'.

Time-marker 'from-yesterday' / 'formerly' (1Sam 4:7; 14:21; 19:7; 21:6; 2Sam 3:17; 5:2; 2Kgs 13:5; Isa 30:33; Mic 2:8). Hyphenated; distinguished phraseologically-adverbially from H8543 temol 'yesterday'.
Woman-says 'this-is-my-hire from lovers'; Hos 2:12.
Proper noun, Gershon-Levi-genealogy; 1Chr 6:41; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ethni.
Specific payment-wage to temple-or-street-prostitutes distinguished from sakhar (work-wage, H7939) (Deut 23:19, Isa 23:17,18, Eze 16:31,34,41, Hos 9:1, Mic 1:7).
Proper noun, son of Helah-Ashur-Tekoa-Judah-branch; 1Chr 4:7; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ethnan.
Aramaic-cognate for location or spot (Ezra 5:15; 6:3,5,7; Dan 2:35). Hyphenated to preserve the Aramaic-parallel of H4725 maqom 'place' (Hebrew).
Proper noun, caravan-road in Negev; Num 21:1; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Atharim.
At-door-entrance stood idol-image; Eze 8:5.
Aramaic-Persian-loan walls-and-foundations (Ezra 4:12, 5:3, 5:9); identity Persian uncertain.
Beer-travel-stop-of-Israel in wilderness and Beer-city-Jotham (Num 21:16,18; Judg 9:21). English convention: Beer-place. Family with H875 beer 'well-spring' (already assigned).
Dug well with water; distinguished from ayin (natural spring); concordantly 'well'.
Num-from-thence-to-Beer-well-of-which-the-LORD-said-to-Moses-gather-the-people-give-them-water and Judg-Jotham-fled-to-Beer (Num 21:16; Judg 9:21). Hyphenated.
Water-cistern at Bethlehem-gate from which David's mighty men drew (2Sam 23:15,16; 1Chr 11:17,18). Hyphenated to distinguish the cistern-water-aspect from homonyms H953a bor-I 'pit' and H1252 bor-II.
Proper noun, Asher tribe-head son of Zophah; 1Chr 7:37; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beera.
Proper noun ('well-of-the-mighty') Moab-border; Isa 15:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beer-elim.
Proper noun, Reuben tribe-head carried away by Tilgath-Pilneser; 1Chr 5:6; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beerah.
Gibeonite city in Benjaminite territory (Josh 9:17; 18:25; 2Sam 4:2; Ezra 2:25; Neh 7:29). English convention: Beeroth. 'Wells'.
Proper noun, Hittite father of Judith; Gen 26:34; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Beeri.
Well of the Living-One-who-sees-me where Hagar and Isaac dwelt (Gen 16:14; 24:62; 25:11). English convention: Beer-Lahai-Roi. Composition 'well-of-the-living-seeing-me', sacred-place-Negev.
Proper noun ('well-of-seven/oath'); city in southern Canaan; concordantly transliterated.
One of the stops of Israel during the wilderness-journey, at the wells of the Jaakan-sons - Deuteronomy 10:6; in Numbers 33:31-32 as Bene-Jaakan.
Designation of inhabitants of Beeroth (2Sam 4:2,5,9; 23:37). Gentilic; family with H881 Be'eroth.
Qal: emit foul odour, become morally repulsive; concordantly 'stink' (also metaphorically 'be-hated').
Aramaic Peal; king-displeased about Daniel-plot; Dan 6:14.
Isa-instead-of-balsam-stench and Joel-stench-of-army-camps and Amos-stench-of-army-camps (Isa 3:24; Joel 2:20; Amos 4:10). Hyphenated.
Hapax Job 31:40 stinkweed-instead-of-wheat; from H889 boshet stench.
Stinking wild grapes - in Isaiah 5:2 (He looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes) and Isaiah 5:4 (why brought it forth wild grapes?).
Whoever-touches-Israel touches-the-apple-of-God's-eye; Zech 2:8.
Priestly family-head after the exile (Ezra 2:11; 8:11; 10:28; Neh 7:16; 10:16). English convention: Bebai.
Proper noun. English convention Babel (not Babylon, which is Greek).
Aramaic proper noun; empire and capital; transliteration, language-marker links to Hebrew Babel.
Aramaic gentilic Babylonians (Ezra 4:9); from H894 Bavel.
Ammon-as-spoil to east-peoples; Eze 25:7.
Qal: break covenant/trust; the hyphenated English compounds 'deal-treacherously'.

Treachery or betrayal - in Isaiah 24:16 (the treacherous deal treacherously, yea, the treacherous deal very treacherously) and Jeremiah 12:1 (why are all who deal treacherously secure?); homograph of beged.
Unique lexeme. Item of clothing. 'Garment' covers both mantle and general robe; 'clothing' is too generic.
Prophets-treacherous in holy-things; Zeph 3:4.
Treacherous or betraying - in Jeremiah 3:7 (and her treacherous sister Judah saw it) and Jeremiah 3:10 (only feignedly, not faithfully); participial adjective of H898 bagad.
Post-exilic family-head returned from Babel (Ezra 2:2,14; 8:14; Neh 7:7,19; 10:17). English convention: Bigvai.
Proper noun, third eunuch attendant of Ahasuerus; Esth 1:10; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bigtha.
One of the two threshold-keeper-eunuchs who plotted against Ahasuerus and were hanged through Mordecai's report - Esther 2:21, 6:2; his fellow-conspirator was Teresh.
Root bdd (be-alone). Mostly with preposition le-vaddo ('to-his-separation' = 'alone'). 'Separation' preserves the nominal form; 'alone' is functional translation of the preposition-complex.
Fine fabric for priestly clothing; distinguished from bad I 'pole/carrying-beam' and III 'alone'; concordantly 'linen'.
Vain-speech or lying inventions (Job 11:3; Isa 16:6; 44:25; Jer 48:30; 50:36). Hyphenated to distinguish the empty-invention-aspect from H3577 kazav 'lie' and H8267 sheqer 'deceit'.

1K-and-he-offered-on-the-altar-which-he-had-made-in-Beth-El-on-the-fifteenth-day-of-the-eighth-month-which-he-had-devised-out-of-his-own-heart and Neh-but-out-of-your-own-heart-you-have-feigned-them (1K 12:33; Neh 6:8).
Solitary-dwell of leper or people (Lev 13:46; Num 23:9; Jer 15:17; Hos 8:9; Ps 102:8). Hyphenated to distinguish the separation-loneliness-aspect from H905 bad 'alone' and H910 badad-adv 'lonely'.
From √badal (separate, H914); state-of-alone-apart-separated (Lev 13:46 leper 'separated shall-he-dwell', Num 23:9 Balaam-on-Israel 'people that dwells apart and is-not-counted-among-nations').
Gen-reigned-Hadad-son-of-Bedad-who-smote-Midian-in-the-field-of-Moab and 1Chr-Hadad-son-of-Bedad (Gen 36:35; 1Chr 1:46). Hyphenated.
Proper noun, son of Bani who took foreign-wife; Ezra 10:35; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bedeiah.
Base metal which is separated-out (Num 31:22; Isa 1:25; Eze 22:18,20; 27:12; Zech 4:10). Hyphenated to preserve the tin-by-metal-aspect.
Hiphil: set apart, divide (cultic: holy from common); Niphal: separate oneself; concordantly 'separate'.
Hapax-form; shepherd-rescues two-feet-pieces from lion's-mouth; Amos 3:12.
Gen-bdellium-land-of-Havilah-gold-and-bdellium-and-onyx-stone and Num-manna-as-bdellium-appearance (Gen 2:12; Num 11:7). Hyphenated.
1S-the-LORD-sent-Jerubbaal-and-Bedan-and-Jephthah-and-Samuel and 1Chr-the-sons-of-Ulam-Bedan-these-were-the-sons-of-Gilead (1S 12:11; 1Chr 7:17). Hyphenated.
Qal-infinitive; temple-renovation under Josiah; 2Chr 34:10.
Crack-in-wall-or-building requiring-repair (2Kgs 12:6,7,8,9,13 Joash-temple-restoration 'repair of-house-of-YHWH', 22:5 = 2Chr 34:10 Josiah's-reforms 'bedeq of-house', 2Chr 34:5).
Proper noun, Jehu's-captain; 2Kgs 9:25; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bidkar.
Aramaic Pael; fruit-tree-scatter; Dan 4:14.

Waste-and-void primaeval-state and judgment-reversal (Gen 1:2; Isa 34:11; Jer 4:23). Hyphenated to distinguish the void-emptiness-chaos-aspect from H8414 tohu 'desolation' (already assigned) and H772 erets.
White-coloured marble in palace of Vashti-feast; Esth 1:6.
Aramaic hurriedness (Ezra 4:23 with-haste to Jerusalem); from √bhl hasten.
Shining-sunlight through clouds-invisible; Job 37:21.
Niphal: suddenly fall into panic; Piel: hurry/hasten; the hyphenated English marks state.
Aramaic cognate of behal (be-terrified, H926); Peal/Pael/Ithpaal: suddenly-startle-or-hurry (Dan 2:25, 3:24, 4:5,19, 5:6,9,10, 7:15,28).
Fright-bewilderment by sickness or judgment (Lev 26:16; Ps 78:33; Isa 65:23; Jer 15:8). Hyphenated to distinguish the dismay-panic-aspect from H2844 chath 'terror' and H368 eymah 'fear'.
Unique lexeme. Four-legged (domestic) animal, collective. 'Beast' covers the generic animal-collectivity; 'cattle' is too narrowly economic.
Giant-animal-Behemoth described by God; Job 40:15.
Thumb or big toe (priest-consecration-blood); concordantly 'thumb'.
Josh-and-the-border-went-up-to-the-stone-of-Bohan-the-son-of-Reuben and Josh-and-the-border-passed-from-the-north-side-to-the-stone-of-Bohan-the-son-of-Reuben (Josh 15:6; 18:17). Hyphenated.
Non-contagious white skin-spot; Lev 13:39.
From √bhr (shine brightly); white/bright skin-patch in diagnostic-procedure Lev 13-14; the hyphenated English marks light-glance + local-phenomenon.
Root bw'. Movement inward or toward. Derivative mavo (entrance, H3996).

Qal: hold for nothing, dismiss with contempt; distinguished from bazah (despise, H959) - buz is the dismissive-contempt-mode (Gen 38:23, Prov 1:7, 6:30, 11:12, 13:13, 14:21, 23:9,22, Neh 2:19, Zech 4:10).
Nominal counterpart of bazah (despise, H959); state-or-object of being-held-in-contempt (Gen 38:23 Judah 'let us be contempt', Job 12:5,21, 31:34, Ps 31:19, 119:22, 123:3,4).
Buz-son-of-Nahor and Israel's-judgment-people (Gen 22:21; Job 32:2,6; Jer 25:23). English convention: Buz. Distinguished from homonym H937 buz-'contempt' (already assigned); Arab-desert-tribe.
Reproach-state Jews at wall-rebuilding; Neh 4:4.
The Aramean tribe from which Elihu's family originated - Job 32:2, 32:6; presumably descended from Buz, son of Nahor (Gen 22:21).
Proper noun, priest-father of Ezekiel; Eze 1:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Buzi.
Proper noun, Levitical wall-rebuilder; Neh 3:18; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bavvai.

Confused-Israelites-in-wilderness and Egyptians-bewildered (Ex 14:3; Joel 1:18; Esth 3:15). Hyphenated to distinguish the confused-trapped-wandering-aspect from H7686 shagah 'wander' (already assigned).

The food-fruit which the mountains bring forth for Behemoth - Job 40:20 (the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play) and Isaiah 44:19 (have I not made the half thereof bread).
Proper noun, eighth month (October/November); 1Kgs 6:38; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bul.
Proper noun, son of Jerahmeel; 1Chr 2:25; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bunah.
Qal/Hithpolel: tread underfoot (Ps 44:6, 60:14, 108:14 'Mighty-One shall trample', 119:118, Prov 27:7, Isa 14:19,25, 63:6,18, Jer 12:10, Eze 16:6, Zech 10:5); concordantly 'trample'.
Late-OT Persian loanword for fine linen (1Chr 4:21; 15:27; 2Chr 2:13; 3:14; 5:12; Esth 1:6; 8:15; Eze 27:16). Hyphenated; distinguished from H8336b shesh-II 'byssus' (Egyptian-variant).
Proper noun, sharp rock-point on Philistine-pass; 1Sam 14:4; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bozez.
Nineveh-emptied-and-laid-waste; Nah 2:10.
Amos-was-herdsman not-prophet's-son; Amos 7:14.
Hapax Eccl 9:1 heart-set-forth-investigate; root √bur-II (not H953 pit).
Hewn-out water-pit or cistern; also used as prison; distinguished from beer (well-spring); concordantly 'pit'.
Second-sense bor; cistern Sirah where Abner went; 2Sam 3:26.
Root bwsh. 'Be-ashamed' preserves the stative shame-state.
Shame-cover at enemy-triumph and sin-result (Ps 89:46; Mic 7:10; Obad 10; Eze 7:18). Hyphenated to distinguish the shame-disgrace-aspect from H2781 cherpah 'reproach-shame' (already assigned).
Aramaic Peal-imperfect; king-passed-night-fasting; Dan 6:18.
From √bazaz (plunder); war-spoil, plundered goods; concordantly 'plunder'.
Cleave or cut through as river through land - in Isaiah 18:2 and Isaiah 18:7 (both occurrences in the expression: a people whose land the rivers divide) - rare verb for geographical division.
Qal: scorn, esteem-low, hold for worthless; concordantly 'despise'.
Despised-servant whom-nations-honour; Isa 49:7.

Abstract-nominal form of bazaz (take-plunder, H962) parallel-with shalal (booty, H7998) but marks acquired-spoils-as-goods-in-possession (2Chr 14:13 Asa 'great spoils-good in-hand', 25:13 substitutes-for).
Qal: rob, plunder, spoil; the hyphenated English marks action plus object.
Women-disdain after Vashti-affair-precedent; Esth 1:18.
Proper noun, Judah-city south; Josh 15:28; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Biziothiah.
Cherubim-moved like lightning-glances; Eze 1:14.
Bezek-city where Judah-Adoni-bezek-defeats and Saul's-monster-numbering (Judg 1:4,5; 1Sam 11:8). English convention: Bezek. 'Splinter' or 'lightning-bolt' (possibly-family-with bazaq-flash).
Scatter and lavishly distribute - in Psalm 68:31 (He scatters peoples that delight in war) and Daniel 11:24 (he shall scatter among them prey, spoil, and goods); intensive action of distributing.
Proper noun, second eunuch attendant of Ahasuerus; Esth 1:10; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Bizzetha.
Jeremiah-as-tester of-people-appointed; Jer 6:27.
Passive participle of bachar (choose): the chosen one, man in the prime of his life; concordantly 'young-man'.

Watchtower or siege-tower - in Isaiah 23:13 (they set up the towers of Assyria against her) and Isaiah 32:14 (the palace shall be forsaken; the multitude of the city shall be left; Ophel and the watchtower).

From √bachar (choose, H977); passive-participle 'one-chosen': Saul's family (2Sam 21:6), Jacob-Israel-status (Ps 105:6,43 = 1Chr 16:13, 106:5, Isa 43:20, 45:4, 65:9,15,22), YHWH-Servant par excellence.
First-sense bachal; my-soul-loathed-them; Zech 11:8.
Second-sense bachal; hastily-acquired-inheritance not-blessed; Prov 20:21.
Qal: investigate-prove, verify (people by YHWH); concordantly 'test'.
City-tower-and-stronghold-become-caves; Isa 32:14.
Zion's-foundation-stone-tested-stone precious; Isa 28:16.
Root bhr. 'Choose' standard.
Patronym-clan David's-warrior Azmaveth; 1Chr 11:33; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Baharumite.
Early-male-age servants of Joshua; Num 11:28.
Benjamite place on road to Jordan (2Sam 3:16; 16:5; 17:18; 19:17; 1Kgs 2:8). English convention: Bahurim. 'Young-men-place'.

Hasty or unconsidered speech without deliberation - in Psalm 106:33 (they provoked his spirit so that he spoke unadvisedly with his lips) and Proverbs 12:18 (there is one who speaks like the piercings of a sword).
Root bth. 'Trust' standard.
From √batach (trust); state of certainty and rest; adverbial 'safely'; concordantly 'safety'.
Proper noun, Aramean place where David seized bronze; 2Sam 8:8; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Betah.
In-quietness-and-trust-your-strength; Isa 30:15.
2K-thus-says-the-great-king-the-king-of-Assyria-what-confidence-is-this-wherein-you-trust and Eccl-for-a-living-dog-is-better-than-a-dead-lion (2K 18:19; Eccl 9:4 cf). Hyphenated.
Tabernacles-of-robbers in security-peace; Job 12:6.
Hapax Eccl 12:3 grinders-ceased-labour; Aramaic-loan also in later Hebrew.
Aramaic-verb for ceasing or halting building-work (Ezra 4:21,23,24; 5:5; 6:8). Hyphenated to mark the Aramaic-parallel; distinguished from Hebrew batel 'cease'.
Anatomical body-part, including womb; concordantly 'belly' (not 'womb' - that is contextual interpretation).
Preposition: 'for', 'through', in protection of; the hyphenated English marks the relation.
Gift from the best of the land; Gen 43:11.
Proper noun, Gad-place; Josh 13:26; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Betonim.
Pleading-interjection: 'with-your-permission, lord' (Judah to Joseph, Moses to YHWH); the hyphenated English marks the polite-address.
Root byn. Discern, understand. 'Discern' preserves the cognitive distinction-action; derived bein (H996), tevunah (H8394).
Root byn (discern, H995). 'Between' holds the distinction-spatial aspect.
Dan-aramaic-between-the-waters and Dan-aramaic-between-horns and Dan-aramaic-between-Daniel-and-Medo-Persia (Dan 7:5,8). Hyphenated.
From √bin; ability to see-through, between-see, clarity-of-understanding; distinguished from tevunah and chokmah; concordantly 'discernment'.
Aramaic parallel to binah; God gives-understanding; Dan 2:21.
Laid eggs of birds or quails (Deut 22:6; Job 6:6; 39:14; Isa 10:14; 59:5). Hyphenated to preserve the bird-egg-product.
Aramaic for fortified palace-stronghold; Ezra 6:2.
Loanword (Persian/Akkadian); fortified palace/citadel (Susa, temple-citadel); the hyphenated English marks the type.
Josh-and-the-border-went-up-to-Beth-Arabah and Josh-Beth-arabah-Zemaraim-and-Bethel (Josh 15:6,61; 18:22). Hyphenated.
